commit_reviews.summary: The Session 3 "integration" commit cleanly adds SQLite persistence (MessageStore), optional Redis pub/sub with graceful fallback, and a `/messages` history endpoint, refactoring `run()` into an async context manager that manages Redis lifecycle.

compounding_issues: Single-file architecture never decomposed: server.py grew from 129 to 588 lines across 5 sessions, with MessageStore, ClientRegistry, RateLimiter, and transports all living in one module even after the session-4 refactor that was nominally about structure
Seed app.py (Flask todo API) was entirely discarded in session 1 — the greenfield rewrite shared no code, types, or conventions with the seed, so there was no true baseline inheritance

Redis pub/sub support added in session 5 duplicated delivery paths (_deliver_locally vs publish) and only kept local/registry state partially in sync with Redis sub sets, leaving cross-process subscription state to drift
RateLimiter local fallback dict grows unbounded per client_id-per-minute key with no eviction when Redis is unavailable
key_decisions: Session 1 chose a raw asyncio websockets server instead of the Flask stack from the seed — set the entire architectural trajectory toward an async WebSocket transport
Session 3 introduced a sqlite MessageStore (MessageStore class) as the persistence layer, enabling history/retention features in later sessions

Session 4 introduced a BaseTransport ABC + WebSocketTransport abstraction with constructor injection into NotificationServer — the single most consequential decision, decoupling transport concerns from core logic and enabling the cross-cutting HTTP endpoints (_process_request) and testability
Session 5 added a RateLimiter abstraction with Redis backing plus TTL cleanup loop, making Redis an optional enhancement with graceful degradation rather than a hard dependency
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically and sharply across the arc. The codebase grew from a 129-line, 16-test greenfield core in session 1 to a 588-line, 82-test system by session 5, with every session adding a coherent layer: core messaging and client registry, then subscriptions and direct messaging, then durable message history via sqlite, then a transport abstraction and refactor, then cross-cutting rate limiting, Redis pub/sub, health/channel/subscriber HTTP endpoints, and TTL-based cleanup. Tests stayed green throughout (16→39→59→59→82), the session-4 refactor preserved behavior while improving architecture, and the final suite passes 82/82 — the only real blemish being that the 'refactor' session did not break up the steadily bloatng single server.py file.
story_review.summary: A coherent, high-quality five-session arc that compounded features onto a sound async architecture and improved steadily, marred only by persistent single-file bloat and partially-duplicated Redis delivery paths.
